audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly sells a "3-stack stun into Devour" combo (spikes[2], wants.you[1], tradeGood, breakdown.trading, dosFull) as the core pattern. That sequence cannot happen.
audit.why: Tongue Lash at 3 stacks stuns AND consumes all three stacks; Devour can only be cast on an enemy carrying 3 stacks and consumes them too. Three stacks buys exactly one payoff — the stun or the eat, never both.
audit.corrected: At 3 stacks you choose: Q for a 1.5s stun, or R to remove him outright. Against Aatrox the eat is almost always correct, because the stun does not stop Umbral Dash or his healing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (P: "At three stacks, he can use Devour"; Q: "they are stunned and the stacks are consumed")

League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench) — "Devour can only be cast on enemies with 3 stacks"; "All three An Acquired Taste stacks will be consumed even if Tongue Lash's stun is negated."

audit.whatIsWrong: "Abyssal Voyage" is named as a level-6 ultimate granting "global escape pressure" and repositioning (spikes[1], spikes[2], wants.you[2], mid x2, whys[3], whys[4]).
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's REMOVED pre-rework ultimate. His current W is Abyssal Dive — a blink available from level 2, on 21/20/19/18/17, that knocks up on arrival. It is not global, not an ultimate, and not an escape you get at 6.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive is live from level 2 as a short-range blink and knockup; the level-6 arrival is Devour.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (W: Abyssal Dive, cd 21/20/19/18/17, range 1000-1200, knockup)
League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states that Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) grounds, and that grounding disables Abyssal Dive.
audit.why: Infernal Chains applies Grounded. Grounded disables movement abilities, and Abyssal Dive is a blink — so while the chain field holds you, your only mobility is switched off. This is the single most decisive kit-vs-kit interaction in the matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Do not hold Abyssal Dive as your escape once Infernal Chains is up — it is disabled while grounded. Blink before he chains, or not at all.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench) — Abyssal Dive listed as disabled by Grounded

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry never connects Aatrox's Deathbringer Stance to Tahm Kench's own itemisation.
audit.why: Deathbringer Stance heals Aatrox based on the TARGET's max health. Tahm Kench stacks max health harder than almost any top laner, so every Heartsteel/Warmog's stack directly increases how much Aatrox heals off him. That reframes the whole "out-sustain him" plan.
audit.corrected: Your HP stacking feeds his passive heal — Grievous Wounds is not optional here, it is the item that makes the attrition plan work at all.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aatrox.json (P: "heals him, based on the target's max health")

audit.whatIsWrong: mid attributes the levels 4-5 sustain to "World Ender passive regen".
audit.why: World Ender is his R and does not exist before level 6. The healing that beats you at 4-5 is Umbral Dash's passive ("Aatrox heals when damaging enemy champions") plus Deathbringer Stance.
audit.corrected: Name Umbral Dash's passive heal at 4-5; World Ender only matters from 6.
sources: champ-data/_kits/aatrox.json (E: "Passively, Aatrox heals when damaging enemy champions"; R cd 120/100/80)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns says "track The Darkin Blade" but never gives a number, so the reader cannot size the window.
audit.why: The Darkin Blade is 14s at rank 1 and only 6s at rank 5 — the punish window collapses as he ranks it. Devour is 120s at rank 1, so it is not a repeatable lane tool.
audit.corrected: Real numbers substituted: Q 14s->6s, Devour 120s at rank 1.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench) — Devour cooldown 120/100/80, cast range 250

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and spikes[2] treat the level-6 Devour as a repeatable "cleanest remove window all game".
audit.why: Devour is on 120s at rank 1 with a 250 cast range. It is a once-per-fight ultimate you walk into melee to use, not a recurring lane pattern.
audit.corrected: Framed as a single committed removal on a 120s cooldown.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench) — Devour cooldown 120/100/80, cast range 250 (Data Dragon reports cooldown 0, which is a data artifact)

notes:
TWO SYSTEMIC ERRORS THAT RUN THROUGH THE WHOLE TAHM KENCH FILE, not just this matchup.

1) "Abyssal Voyage" appears 182 times in champ-data/content/tahmkench.js and 0 times in champ-data/tahmkench.full.js. "Abyssal Dive" appears 0 times. Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's REMOVED pre-rework ultimate; the current W is Abyssal Dive (blink + knockup, cd 21/20/19/18/17, available from level 2). Almost every occurrence is wrong twice over — wrong name AND wrong slot, because the text treats it as a level-6 global repositioning ultimate. This needs a file-wide pass well beyond my 8-matchup slice.

2) The "3-stack stun into Devour" combo is sold across the file as Tahm Kench's core pattern and it is mechanically impossible. Tongue Lash at 3 stacks stuns and consumes all three stacks; Devour requires 3 stacks on the target and consumes them. You get the stun OR the eat. Confirmed against Riot's own ability text in champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json and against the League Wiki. I fixed the instances inside my slice; the same phrasing recurs across the other ~63 matchups.

3) DATA ARTIFACT: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json lists Devour's cooldown as "0" and its range as "25000". Both are Data Dragon placeholders. The real values are cooldown 120/100/80 and cast range 250. Anything downstream that derived "Devour is low cooldown" from the kit file is wrong.

4) Aatrox's R World Ender carries a "hardCC" flag in champ-data/_kits/aatrox.json, but Riot's text only fears MINIONS — it applies no CC to champions. Do not let that flag generate champion-CC advice.

5) STALE ITEM: spikes[3] and late build Aatrox's power curve around Goredrinker, which no longer exists on patch 26.15. I did not propose a replacement because I could not verify the current Aatrox first item and will not invent an item name. Recommend an itemisation pass across this file.

6) LAYER DISAGREEMENT: full.diff is "EVEN" (6/10) and full.phases hands Tahm Kench 4 of 7 stages, while the packet win rate is 46.73% over 1408 games and the content-layer chart hands Aatrox 5 of 7. I could not fix either: "EVEN"->"TRICKY" and the phases[].side champion names both blow the +/-10% length band. This needs the applier to allow short-field edits, or a manual pass.
